title: Filtered projective model for filtered-origin endomorphisms
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, and call an object of the ordinary module derived category $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] perfect when it is isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] $A$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Let $DF_2(A)$ be the localization of the homotopy category of pairs of cochain complexes $K'\subset K$ at the filtration-preserving chain maps that induce quasi-isomorphisms on $K'$ and $K/K'$; homotopies are maps $h^i:K^i\to L^{i-1}$ with $f-g=dh+hd$ and $h^i(K'^i)\subseteq L'^{i-1}$. Thus the filtration is $0\subset K'\subset K$, with the two graded pieces defined by subcomplex and quotient [def-sp-filtration, def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. Suppose $\mathcal P\in DF_2(A)$ has perfect graded pieces, and let $u:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P$ be any endomorphism in this localized category. Then there are bounded complexes $M'\subset M$ and $M''=M/M'$ of finitely generated projective $A$-modules, an isomorphism $(M'\subset M)\cong\mathcal P$ in $DF_2(A)$, and a filtration-preserving chain endomorphism $\bar u$ of $(M'\subset M)$ whose localized image is $u$ under this isomorphism. The exact sequence $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ splits in every cochain degree. The restricted and quotient chain endomorphisms represent the endomorphisms induced by $u$ on the two graded pieces. Here filtration-preserving means $\bar u(M')\subseteq M'$; it does not assert that $\bar u(F^iM)=\operatorname{im}(\bar u)\cap F^iM$.

proof.text: Choose a literal mono of complexes K′ → K representing P: both the homotopy quotient and its localization are bijective on objects. Its cokernel K″ gives a short exact sequence of complexes and hence a distinguished triangle Q(K′) → Q(K) → Q(K″). The two graded perfectness hypotheses say that the first and third vertices are perfect. By [lem-sf-perfect-ring-triangle-closure], Q(K) is perfect as well.

source.place: Tag 066R, two-out-of-three perfect complexes; ordinary triangle of a short exact sequence

proof.text: By [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], choose bounded finite-projective complexes X,Y and derived isomorphisms Q(X) ≅ Q(K′), Q(Y) ≅ Q(K). Bounded-above projectivity makes X,Y K-projective. The surjectivity of [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative] represents these isomorphisms by chain maps a:X→K′ and b:Y→K. They are quasi-isomorphisms since their derived images are invertible. The same surjectivity gives g:X→Y representing the inclusion transported through these isomorphisms. The injectivity gives a homotopy between a followed by K′→K and g followed by b.

source.place: Tags 014E/014F; K-projective Hom bijection supplies the homotopy-commuting square

proof.text: Let C=cone(id_X), T=C⊕Y, and i:X→T have components the cone inclusion and g. Put δ=a·inclusion−g·b. The homotopy of step 2 is a null homotopy of δ; the cone universal construction gives t:C→K restricting to δ on X. Then q=(t,b):T→K satisfies i·q=a·inclusion exactly. In degree n, projection Tⁿ→Cⁿ followed by the cone second-coordinate projection Cⁿ→Xⁿ retracts iⁿ, so i is monic. This construction rectifies the square as a genuine filtered map, without identifying filtered objects solely by their triangles.

source.place: Tags 014E (definition-cone) and 014F (lemma-functorial-cone), explicit cone universal construction

proof.text: The complex C=cone(id_X) is contractible, so the inclusion Y→T is a homotopy equivalence. Its composite with q equals b, hence q is a quasi-isomorphism. Apply two-out-of-three for the homology sequences of the short exact rows X→T→coker(i) and K′→K→K″ to obtain a quasi-isomorphism on cokernels. Thus (a,q) is a filtered quasi-isomorphism and gives the desired filtered derived isomorphism j. The terms of T are Xⁿ⁺¹⊕Xⁿ⊕Yⁿ; finite generation and projectivity follow from finite direct sums. The degreewise retraction of i splits the quotient, whose terms are therefore finite projective direct summands of Tⁿ. If X,Y have bounds [ax,bx],[ay,by], all three complexes have common bounds [min(ax,ay)−1,max(bx,by)]; the quotient bounds follow from the epi Tⁿ→coker(i)ⁿ. This includes zero complexes and the zero ring.

source.place: Tags 014E/014F; the long exact homology sequences of the two short exact rows

proof.text: Apply the two-step unrestricted-target Hom bijection of [lem-trf-filtered-projective-comparison] to the bounded-above graded-projective model M=(X→T). Represent j·u·j⁻¹ by a homotopy class v, then choose a literal filtered chain-map representative ū of v. Cancel j⁻¹·j to get Q(ū)·j=j·u.

source.place: Tag 03TJ, with the two-step unrestricted-target comparison supplied by the comparison node

proof.text: The canonical graded functors are the localization lifts of the subcomplex and cokernel functors. The localization factorization and homotopy-quotient lift give Q₂ followed by gr_c = grComplex_c followed by ordinary Q, on objects and morphisms. Apply gr_c to the conjugacy equation of step 5, and use this factorization to obtain the two required graded conjugacy equations.

lean.statement: theorem exists_filteredProjectiveModel {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} A)] (P : TwoStepModuleDerived A) (hP : ∀ c : Bool, DerivedCategory.IsPerfectRingComplex ((twoStepGraded A c).obj P)) (uP : P ⟶ P) : ∃ M : TwoStepModuleComplex A, (∃ a b : ℤ, M.obj.right.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ M.obj.right.IsStrictlyLE b ∧ ∀ c : Bool, ((twoStepGradedComplex A c).obj M).IsStrictlyGE a ∧ ((twoStepGradedComplex A c).obj M).IsStrictlyLE b) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, (Module.Finite A (M.obj.right.X n) ∧ Module.Projective A (M.obj.right.X n)) ∧ ∀ c : Bool, Module.Finite A (((twoStepGradedComplex A c).obj M).X n) ∧ Module.Projective A (((twoStepGradedComplex A c).obj M).X n)) ∧ (ShortComplex.mk M.obj.hom (cokernel.π M.obj.hom) (cokernel.condition M.obj.hom)).ShortExact ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ s : (cokernel M.obj.hom).X n ⟶ M.obj.right.X n, s ≫ (cokernel.π M.obj.hom).f n = 𝟙 _) ∧ ∃ j : (twoStepModuleQ A).obj M ≅ P, ∃ ū : M ⟶ M, (twoStepModuleQ A).map ū ≫ j.hom = j.hom ≫ uP ∧ ∀ c : Bool, DerivedCategory.Q.map ((twoStepGradedComplex A c).map ū) ≫ (twoStepGraded A c).map j.hom = (twoStepGraded A c).map j.hom ≫ (twoStepGraded A c).map uP
